summary.pass_bar: MET: recall 1.0 (7/7, current gold set), control 0, schema 0, contradictions 0, tiny 0, < 2 s. The 10 extra changes are the same as before the QA fixes and were all checked against the frames (listed below). QA fixes changed no detection's kind, metric or years; only region descriptions and one persistence (Palm vegetation_gain 3 -> 4, now counted on the NDVI series it is told on).

method: Place-wide layer: the segments approach unchanged (despike, BIC-chosen straight segments, movements >= max(physical floor, 4 x noise), lasting >= 2 summers, one connected patch >= 1% of the area).

Local layer: per pixel, built-up must FULLY flip between the 3 summers before and the 3 after (never built in any clear summer before, built in every clear summer after, or the reverse; >= 2 clear summers per window). Connected (8-neighbour) patches >= 4 ha. Same pixels at splits <= 2 apart are one event.

Local magnitude is measured INSIDE the patch's region: mean built-up share of the region's pixels over the 3 summers after minus the 3 before (about +/-1.0 for a full flip). The narration must say 'in this area'. This replaces window-means' share of the whole 6 km square, which made real local changes tiny (0.001-0.006).

Local changes also need: the old state seen for 6 summers (3 before the before-window that sit on the old side), persistence >= 2 summers (FR-22), and, if dated within 1 year of a sensor switch, >= 2 later summers clear of every switch that stay changed (otherwise dropped; if kept, sensor_switch_flag is set, DR-6).

Local re-reads: a rise on pixels that were water -> exposed shore (dropped if a place-wide water_loss tells it, else re-told as water_loss on the region's water share); a rise inside a burn -> dropped; a fall that became water -> water_gain likewise; a fall in an arid place -> dropped (desert rule); a fall whose region greened >= 0.1 NDVI -> told as vegetation_gain on the region's land NDVI (what is visible), not as built-up falling.
Same-kind local changes <= 500 m apart with start years <= 2 apart are merged and re-measured over the joined region.

Final honesty gate: kind, metric and sign must agree (water_loss/-, water_gain/+, vegetation_loss/-, vegetation_gain/+, burn/-, urban_growth on built_frac/+, other on built_frac/-); anything else is dropped, never re-signed.
Ranking: place-wide first (by size in noise units), then local by area x |in-region magnitude|; keep 5 (HL-2).

summerlin_decision.choice: vegetation_gain on ndvi_mean, 1991-2019, +0.107, region 'in the east part of the area, where bare dry ground turned greener'. The built_frac fall is not reported.
why: Checked per pixel (1986-88 vs 2010-12): 0 pixels go from not built-up to built-up; 25,860 go the other way. Bare desert passes the built-up test and roofs, roads and lawns score lower, so urban_growth on built_frac with a positive magnitude does not exist in our data. Urban_growth with a negative magnitude (or on ndvi_mean) would be a contradiction.
'other' on built_frac with a negative magnitude is what the film tells as demolition, which is false here.

Greenness really rose (place land NDVI 0.10 -> 0.21; 70% of the pixels that left 'built-up' gained >= 0.05 NDVI) and the frames show it: 1991 is bare desert, 2019 is streets, parks and golf-course green. So vegetation_gain is a true, visible statement; the sources can then say why (development).
It is dated and placed by the clearer built-up fall (same pixels, same years), as segments did, but keeps the NDVI number so the chart and script agree.
summerlin_decision.arid_test: median yearly land NDVI over the whole record < 0.2 (Summerlin 0.16, Palm Jumeirah 0.07). The whole record, because irrigated suburbs lift Summerlin above 0.2 after 2013 and a recent-window test let a 2017-18 subdivision through as 'other' (demolition).

misses.note: None on the current gold set (7/7). The earlier misses (Lake Mead 2023 water_gain, Summerlin as urban_growth, Willow Run runway) are no longer gold entries; the reasons they can't be found honestly still hold if they come back.

thresholds.PHYSICAL_FLOOR / NOISE_K / SPIKE_K / MAX: unchanged from segments/ (0.03 NDVI, 0.02 of the area; 4 x noise; 3 x noise spikes; <= 6 segments of >= 3 years; place-wide patch >= 1% of the area).
thresholds.WINDOW = 3: 3 summers per side average out one odd summer and still date a change to about a year (both prior approaches settled on 3).
thresholds.LOCAL_MIN_PATCH_HA = 4: about 44 pixels: a big-box store with its car park, a bridge plaza. The control's largest fully flipped patch at any split is 23 px (~2 ha), so a 2x margin. Sweep: 2.5 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 ha all keep the control at 0; 2.5-3 ha adds Summerlin infill and a Ypsilanti patch, 5-6 ha loses Willow Run and Delray patches.
thresholds.full flip (0 of the clear summers before: a single patch has to prove the change alone; 2-of-3 flips give the control patches of up to 296 px (~27 ha).
thresholds.old state seen for 6 summers: one patch is weak evidence; an odd first summer (Willow Run 1984, built 0.10 vs 0.07) made two 1986-87 patches that were a new dark roof and bare soil re-greening.
thresholds.PERSIST_MIN = 2: FR-22; one odd summer is forgiven, two in a row end the count. Burns need 1 (sudden; the dNBR test already rules out haze).
thresholds.sensor rule: change dated within 1 year of a main-sensor switch (TM -> ETM+-only -> OLI) needs >= 2 later summers clear of any switch that stay changed, else dropped (dropped: Delray 2011-12). Kept ones carry sensor_switch_flag.
thresholds.LOCAL_GREENING_MIN = 0.10: the same 'visible' NDVI step as the place-wide pixel test; the built-up test cannot tell a removed roof from bare soil that grew over, so a region that turned green is told as greening.
thresholds.MERGE_GAP_M = 500, MERGE_YEARS = 2: a cleared block and the plaza next to it are one project (Delray 2019-21: 168 px + 86 px + 59 px -> one 28 ha change).
thresholds.BURN_DNBR_MIN = 0.27, BURN_MAX_YEARS = 2: USGS moderate severity; measured on the first summer after the drop began (Paradise: 0.31 in 2019, 0.25 by 2020 as plants regrow).
thresholds.WATER_SHARE = 0.5, DESERT_NDVI_MAX = 0.2: as in the prior approaches (shrinking-lake rule; arid land; greening).

real: water covers the east shore's coves again by 1998.

check_images_how: python spikes/s3-changes/combined/make_check_images.py [place keys]: per change, whole before/after frames and a close-up (>= 1.2 km) with the region box.
weaknesses: Built-up = bare soil too. Local 'urban_growth' patches are often land cleared for building, not finished buildings (Delray 2015-16, Willow Run 2001-02). The kind stays urban_growth (the schema has no 'cleared' kind) but the region description now says 'where land was cleared or built over'; the script must not say 'built' unless a source does.

Local magnitudes are in-region (about +/-1.0). The script must say 'in this area' and never present them as a share of the whole place; the schema has no field that says which, so the promoted code needs a flag or a convention (proposal: region.scope = 'local' | 'place', needs a contract change agreed with Vanessa).

Built-up falls outside deserts are only told when they visibly greened; a real demolition that left bare ground or rubble is dropped (only a local, fully flipped fall with no greening is kept as 'other', e.g. Willow Run 2013-14). Safer than narrating fields as demolition.
Thin features (runways, roads, shorelines) under ~2 pixels wide cannot form a 4 ha fully flipped patch.
The arid test is place-wide (median NDVI < 0.2). A place that is half desert, half irrigated farmland may be misjudged.
The 4 ha floor and 6-summer history rule are set against one control; local changes in the first 6 summers of the record (1984-1989) can't be found.
Shrinking-lake and desert rules re-tell or drop changes; a real town on an old lake bed would be told as water_loss or not at all.
Region bbox maps pixels linearly to place.bbox (UTM square vs lon/lat envelope): off by at most a pixel or two.
Only 7 scored places; thresholds are physical but untested on forests, farms, snow.
qa_fixes: Place-wide built-up falls are never kept as 'other' (demolition). Arid places: desert rule as before. Elsewhere: if the same pixels greened >= 0.10 NDVI over the same years, re-told as vegetation_gain on ndvi_mean (unless an overlapping greening change already tells it); otherwise dropped. On the gold set this dropped falls at Paradise (greened 0.047), Central Park (0.02, 0.087) and Willow Run 1984-93 (greened 0.111 per pixel, but place-wide NDVI +0.056 < its size bar 0.070); none of them reached the output before either.

Every re-told change (shrinking lake -> water_loss, local -> water_loss/water_gain, local -> vegetation_gain, desert greening re-dated by the built-up fall) must now pass the physical floor and NOISE_K x noise of the series it is told on, not just have the right sign. A re-dated desert greening that fails keeps its own years and number.

The sensor-switch rule (within 1 year of a switch -> >= 2 later switch-free summers that stay changed, else dropped) now applies to place-wide changes too, as in ADR-003. Lake Mead 2013-14 and Palm 2002-19 pass it.
urban_growth regions now read '..., where land was cleared or built over'. Local phrases are 'a N ha area in the east part', '... near the centre', '... spread across the place'.
